# unrecognized / inherently unsafe commands
rm -rf /
curl http://evil.example.com
sudo rm -rf /

# code-capable tools with no per-flag allow-list (can execute via their own primitives)
awk '{print $1}' file.txt
awk 'BEGIN{system("rm -rf /")}'
sed 's/a/b/' file.txt
sed '1e id'

# commands that write or execute through their own flags or operands
sort -o out.txt file
sort -oout.txt file
sort --output=out.txt file
sort --compress-program=sh file
uniq file.txt out.txt
uniq - out.txt
tree -o out.txt
less +!sh x
less -o out x
date -s "2020-01-01"
date 010112002020
hostname newhost
hostname -F file

# find with forbidden flags
find . -name "*.sh" -exec rm {} \;
find . -execdir ls \;
find . -prune
find . -delete
find . -fprint out.txt
find . -fprint0 out.txt

# escaped flags must still resolve to the forbidden flag they spell
find . -e\xec rm {} \;

# uname/ps without the specific required args
uname
uname -r
ps
ps -ef

# command substitution / subshells are treated as unsafe
echo $(rm -rf /)
cat `whoami`
(rm -rf /)
(ls)(pwd)

# process substitution spawns a subprocess as a plain argument
diff a.txt <(rm -rf /)
cat <(rm -rf /)

# background execution and newline-separated commands must not be absorbed as args
ls & rm -rf /

# compound commands where at least one part is unsafe
ls -la && rm -rf /
find . -delete | grep foo

# redirection on an earlier segment is still checked
ls > ~/.bashrc && pwd
cat file.txt > /usr/bin/evil | grep foo
ls > out.txt ; rm -rf /
ls ; curl http://evil.example.com
